#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This change covers these cases that probes could be started or stopped:
1. pod creation,  static pod  KILL -> CREATE or soft admission failured last sync, syncPod guarantees probes have started
2. soft admission failure, syncPod guarantees probes are stopped
3. pod deletion, static pod removal, node-shutdown, pod eviction or pod preemption, syncTerminatedPod guarantees probes are stopped.

AddPod and RemovePod of probeManager are all reentrant, so we don't change these interfaces

issue_context.title: Eviction and soft admission failures should stop pod probes
issue_context.body:
The only places pod probes are being managed are HandlePodAdd/HandlePodRemove, but there are other lifecycle changes that cause probes to need to stop (evict, soft admission failures, static pod restart).  The podManager calls should be moved inside sync*Pod and be made reentrant - syncPod should guarantee probes have started, syncTerminatingPod and syncTerminatedPod should guarantee they are stopped.

Discovered while fixing #104847 - we need test cases that guarantee that probes stop when the pod should not be running

review_comments: I think ultimately probe manager responsibilities should be moved completely to pod worker.  Do you believe that cannot be done?  Pod worker is "running pods" and owns the complete responsibility for all pod lifecycle, so it should be the one coordinating other elements of "must run" and "reconcile to ensure a pod is running".

By in pod worker, i mean in one of the three sync*Pod methods, which are guaranteed to be called at specific points in the pod lifecycle.

* syncPod repeateadly called when a pod should be running
* syncTerminatingPod called at least once to stop a pod's containers
* syncTerminatedPod called at least once after all pod containers are stopped

Note that syncPod handles soft admission (softAdmission is when a pod is stopped because a temporary condition prevents it running) so it already has responsibility for stopping "all background kubelet processes related to the pod".

Hard admission of an already admitted pod is guaranteed to call the pod worker to syncTerminatedPod (probably, if not we should fix that so syncTerminatedPod gets at least one chance to run)

> I think ultimately probe manager responsibilities should be moved completely to pod worker. Do you believe that cannot be done? Pod worker is "running pods" and owns the complete responsibility for all pod lifecycle, so it should be the one coordinating other elements of "must run" and "reconcile to ensure a pod is running".

Yea, do you mean that we should control probeManager calls completely inside podworker?  not inside the three sync*Pod methods?

> Note that syncPod handles soft admission (softAdmission is when a pod is stopped because a temporary condition prevents it running) so it already has responsibility for stopping "all background kubelet processes related to the pod".
> 
> Hard admission of an already admitted pod is guaranteed to call the pod worker to syncTerminatedPod (probably, if not we should fix that so syncTerminatedPod gets at least one chance to run)

For softAdmission,  we request the pod's containers be stopped,  This is not the same as termination (we want to stop the pod, but potentially restart it later if soft admission allows it later), we can only stop probles in syncPod

For Hard admission, if the pod has not ever be created, we don't need control probles, because they have not been started yet; if the pod already admitted, then the pod becomes Failed, it would be teardown, then we still could stop probles in syncTerminatingPod and syncTerminatedPod

> Yea, do you mean that we should control probeManager calls completely inside podworker? not inside the three sync*Pod methods?

No, I meant calling them only inside sync*Pod.
